judgements.justification: A's two-sentence meta-review follows its reviewers' themes and B's acceptance follows its scores; neither AC set the outcome from their own reading.
No reviewer or AC on either side rested the recommendation on a forecast of broad impact.
The 11 August replies moved B's RJD5 from 4 to 6 and yRN6 to 7, while no A reviewer replied and A's mean stayed at 4.75.
Each committee had one thin review (A's MjL3, B's yRQF), and B's RJD5 wrote the most exact review on either side; neither committee as a whole was thin.
Only A raised the uncited degree-debiasing literature (APPR, Lasagne, Fairwalk, role2vec, DEMO-Net), and A's meta-review lists novelty and missing comparisons as reasons to reject.
Both committees saw the same Fig. 3 results, with Glove ahead on three of six graphs; A called it no clear superiority, B accepted 'the best or nearly the best'.
B's raises cite the authors' edits and new baselines, not other reviewers' views, and A had no visible discussion.
A's Reviewer_MjL3 wrote only praise with no weakness or question yet rated 6, the borderline accept level.
No reviewer on either side gave a borderline score for want of expertise; B's self-declared non-expert yRQF gave 8.
B's meta-review does not adopt yRQF's verdict and borrows its closing phrase from eKFw; A's follows the majority.
The verbal assessments differed in substance (A: novelty and missing comparisons; B: valued insight), so this is not one verdict scored at two levels.
Neither committee was unanimous; B's spotlight came with a spread of 6, 6, 8, 7.
B's raises rested on new experiments the authors ran on the paper's own setup and on conceded corrections, not on copied results; R16 covers the mechanism.
B's meta-review called the concerns 'mostly regarding the presentation', which drops RJD5's train-test leak fix and the offset-only result at 96% of r2v's AUC.
A's Reviewer_2mkY wrongly said Glove is 'consistently performing better', and B's champion yRQF wrongly said r2v 'works empirically the best'; each claim fed that reviewer's score.
B heard the authors concede that the degree offset alone reaches 96% of r2v's AUC and that node2vec beats r2v-dcSBM on impact factor after the leak fix, yet RJD5 raised from 4 to 6.
No objection or score cut came after the response period; MjL3's late edit is an acknowledgment only.
The scores differ widely (mean 4.75 against 6.75), so the split does not come from tier cut-offs on similar scores.
A's most expert reviewer, HWNH (confidence 5), was negative and A's AC followed that view; B's AC did not pass over RJD5's final 6.
A's main concerns (missing baselines and related work) were answerable, and the authors did answer them with Fairwalk, GAT and new text; A simply did not reply.
Without B's 8 the remaining scores (6, 6, 7) still do not match A's 4, 5, 4, so one outlier did not set the split.
B's outlier yRQF did not reply, but its positive score was not one the response answered; A had no outlier.
Neither AC set aside a detractor and framed the decision as accept or reject.
No reviewer on either side raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review lists 'lacking comparison' though the rebuttal added Fairwalk and GAT, and says the discussion 'converged on rejection' with no discussion on the forum and MjL3 at 6.
No A reviewer answered the 11 August replies, while B's RJD5 and yRN6 engaged over two rounds and raised.
B's Reviewer_yRQF said it would 'rely on other reviewers to judge the originality' yet rated 8, and B's AC counted it in the mean behind the spotlight.
A's scores 4, 5, 4, 6 are not an even split, and B had no split.
The notes show both committees got long replies with new baselines and no conflicting numbers or one-sided concessions.
A's novelty concern rests on real, relevant omitted work, and no B reviewer endorsed a 'first' claim; R05 covers the gap.
B's spotlight on 6, 6, 8, 7 has no stated grounds in the meta-review, and no reviewer argued for a highlight.
Neither committee's critics argued from a neighbouring field's premises against the paper's framing.
B's only score above 7 came from a light five-sentence review with no reply after the rebuttal, so neither committee had an engaged champion above the accept level.
No reviewer or AC rejected the fixes as too large to accept without another review.
A's AC cites a discussion not visible on the forum, but no off-record reviewer's verdict settled a split.
A judged the paper by state-of-the-art performance, which the authors asked q94Z not to use, while B accepted that understanding the degree bias, not accuracy, is the contribution.

reasoning: The split has four parts, and existing reasons cover each one. First, A judged the paper against degree-debiasing work that only A raised (R05). Second, both committees saw the same mixed Fig. 3 results but weighed them differently (R06), and A asked for state-of-the-art performance where B valued the insight (R36). Third, B's reviewers engaged with the rebuttal and A's did not (R03, R26). B also kept its raises after damaging concessions on the offset-only baseline and the leak fix (R16). Fourth, B's spotlight rests on a non-expert 8 with no stated grounds for the tier (R27, R31). Both meta-reviews misreport their record (R14, R25), and reviewers on both sides misread Fig. 3 (R15). The candidate 'score raises for conceded corrections' is R03 plus R16, so the pair adds no reason.
